mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing this fact allows TaskDeletion atoms to exist with no corresponding DeleteOperation, breaking the append-only invariant. The injection then forces a free-floating (unanchored) TaskDeletion to exist, which AppendOnly and FR_018_DeletionLogged should catch.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AppendOnlyViolation { some td: TaskDeletion | no do: DeleteOperation | do.logEntry = td }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing this fact removes the constraint that editing a Done task requires a simultaneous status transition. The injection then forces an EditOperation targeting a Done task with no newStatus change, exactly the violation FR-011 prohibits.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_ClosedTaskViolation { some eo: EditOperation | eo.target.status = Done and no eo.newStatus }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing this fact removes the requirement that a DeleteOperation's log entry is attributed to its caller. The injection forces a mismatch between deleter and caller, violating attribution correctness and audit completeness.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AttributionViolation { some do: DeleteOperation | some m: Member | m != do.caller and do.logEntry.deletedBy = m }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing this fact allows the PermMatrix.Allowed relation to be any subset of Member × OperationKind, including one where some member is denied some operation. The injection then forces a missing cell, directly violating the flat peer invariant.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_FlatPermViolation { some m: Member | some ok: OperationKind | m -> ok not in PermMatrix.Allowed }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing this fact allows a Task's assignee to be any atom, not necessarily a Member. The injection then forces a Task to have an assignee outside the Member sig, violating both the membership constraint and the exclusivity invariant.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AssigneeViolation { some t: Task | some x: (Task - Member) | t.assignee = x }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing this fact removes the guarantee that every Task has a creator. The injection then forces a Task whose creator is not a Member (i.e., the creator field references a non-member atom), violating FR-009's requirement that the creator always records the authenticated identity.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_CreatorViolation { some t: Task | t.creator not in Member }
